concerns.text: The variance‑filter step retains at most `min(N‑1, 200)` bins per cell line (where N = #samples). With only five cell lines (N=5) this leaves ≤ 4 bins, yet later the plan evaluates the “percentage of top‑100 bins within ±10 kb” (Phase 7) and expects SC‑003 (≥ 80 % of top‑100 within ±10 kb). The analysis of top‑100 bins is impossible with ≤ 4 retained bins, creating a methodological inconsistency and rendering the enrichment claim unsound.

The study relies on a sample size of five cell lines (one RNA‑seq and ATAC/DNase sample per line) to train Elastic Net models with 200 candidate predictors. Even after variance filtering, the predictor‑to‑sample ratio remains extreme, leading to severe over‑fitting and insufficient statistical power. No power analysis or justification for the chosen sample size is provided, so the ability to detect meaningful predictive signal is questionable.

Promoter regions (±2 kb) are explicitly set to zero and excluded from the feature matrix. Promoter accessibility is a well‑established determinant of transcriptional output; omitting it may compromise construct validity of the “chromatin accessibility” predictor and bias the model toward distal signals that may be weaker predictors.
